newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Electricidad drags Caracas stks despite rate drop.
newsitem.headline: Electricidad drags Caracas stks despite rate drop.

text.p: A morning sell-off in market- leading utility Electricidad de Caracas dragged Caracas stocks, which closed the day gently off despite a nearly one percentage point fall in interest rates, brokers said.
"A foreign group sold some five million Electricidad shares, which brought the rest of the morning market down," said Inverworld broker Luis Benshimol.
However the fall brought out strong buyers, firming the stock, which closed up 1.75 bolivars on the day at 502.75.
"There was good support at 495 bolivars," said Benshimol.

The market's .IBC index fell 0.51 percent to close at 5,957.78 points as 22 shares fell, 14 rose and six closed flat. Traders said the fall in benchmark six-month interest rates to a year-low of 13.42 percent at today's 130 billion bolivar auction of Central Bank TEMs had no effect on the market.
A total of 17.5 million shares traded, worth 4.4 billion bolivars ($9.4 million).

Among other widely held shares, telephone company CANTV lost 48.50 bolivars to end at 1770.00, steel company Sivensa gained 2.90 to end at 309.90 and foods producer Mavesa lost 1.75 bolivars to close at 132.25 bolivars.
